children: Las Vegas Sands had a lower profit in the third quarter due to falling casino revenue.
The resort and casino company on Wednesday said profit fell to $304 million, or 48 cents a share, from $419 million, or 61 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted per-share earnings were 54 cents, behind the 68 cents anticipated by analysts, according to FactSet.
Third-quarter revenue fell 3.5% to $3.22 billion. Analysts surveyed by FactSet forecast revenue of $3.33 billion.
Sales from casinos, which make up the bulk of revenue, fell 5%. Revenue from rooms, food and beverage, and malls all increased.
Shares were down about 3% to 36.40 in after-hours trading.
